name: ideal_gas_tank_blowdown
title: Emptying an adiabatic tank filled with an ideal gas
summary: Rigid adiabatic tank of ideal gas (air, constant heat capacities) blown down from 100 psi to ambient 14.7 psi: the isentropic-type relation on absolute temperatures T_2_K = T_1_K*(P_2/P_1)^(R/c_P) gives the final tank temperature, from 20 C to about -104 C.

origin.notes: Example 4.5-2 of Klein & Nellis, Thermodynamics (Cambridge University Press, 2011); EES example (c) F-Chart Software, MIT via EES-Community/ees-examples. The binary .eez companion (EES 11.912) carries the stored solution used as verification reference. Original download page in the file header: https://fchartsoftware.com/ees/examples/examples_thermodynamics_2011/chapter%204/example%204.5-2.eez

verification.summary: Compared with the EES solution stored in the .eez companion of the source file (7 common variables with --ees-units, --all): 0 differ at rtol 0.001; largest printed relative deviation 1.51e-05 on R (molar mass of Air, EES vs CoolProp) and 9.66e-06 on T_2. Stored point recomputed by hand: 293.15*0.147^(287.043/1004.643) = 169.50351 K matches the stored T_2.
verification.reference: EES stored solution (8 variables) of the .eez companion ees-examples-raw/uncategorized/example_4.5-2.eez (EES 11.912), compared with tools/compare_solution.py --ees-units --all
verification.notes: Tool summary: '7 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 1; only in CoolSolve: 3'. The only-in-EES variable is P_2_psi (dropped by the unit conversion, its value 14.7 psi is kept as the P_2 input). The only-in-CoolSolve variables are T_1_K, T_2_K (added by the °C storage of temperatures) and R#.
